thread:
anna: heads up — we had a weird eviction wave in ap-southeast1 last night that correlated with a sudden egress quota bump on a subset of racks. lots of tiny pods got scattered instead of packing, ended up wasting GPU slices and causing preempts.

mike: saw that in the SRE alerts, looked like chaining evictions from warm pools. can you paste the kube events or logs?

anna: here's the snippet from the node events: 
```
Warning  Eviction  2m   kubelet  pod sandbox evicted: node egress quota exceeded, nic throttled
Normal   PodPreempted  1m  scheduler  Preempted pod uid=... for gpu-request=1
```

lena: interesting — this matches the cross-az egress-saturation incidents earlier, but this was localized to a single rack's top-of-rack switch and our egress policy routed some model-training traffic out-of-region briefly. those training jobs request fractional gpus so scheduler keeps scattering them.

ji: scheduler perspective: current scoring only considers gpu_fit, cpu_fit, and locality. we don't penalize nodes with high egress-util, so when egress hits a threshold, we get forced rebinds. proposal: add an "egress-penalty" score weight that increases linearly after node.egress_bytes > X.

mike: adding scoring sounds reasonable, but worried about oscillation — if we suddenly mark nodes as bad, a bunch of small pods get rescheduled and make it worse. any mitigation ideas?

anna: thought about a short-lived burstpool concept: a small reserved set of nodes (burstpool) that accept pods which can tolerate lower egress SLAs and be preempted in exchange for better packing on the main fleet. autoscaler would spin these up only during high egress pressure.

lena: love the idea, because it isolates churn. cost tradeoff: burstpools would be cheaper instances but still GPU-backed; we can cap their time-to-live and only use for low-priority fractional workloads.

ji: implementation sketch for scoring change (pseudo config):
```
schedulerConfig:
  scoring:
    - name: gpu_fit
      weight: 100
    - name: locality
      weight: 50
    - name: egress_penalty
      weight: 40
      params:
        threshold_bytes: 1000000000 # 1GB in 5m
        linear_factor: 0.00000005
```
The egress_penalty returns a negative score when node.egress_5m > threshold_bytes.

mike: could we instead make it hysteretic? like only apply penalty if the node has been above threshold for >2 windows, and cool down 10m after it drops. avoids flip-flop.

ji: yes, add two more params: sustained_windows and cooldown_seconds, easy to add to scoring plugin.

anna: ops plan:
- ji to prototype scoring plugin in staging (2 days)
- lena to sketch burstpool autoscaler config + cost estimate (1 day)
- mike to add SLOs and eviction playbook for low-priority pods (half day)

mike: one more: telemetry. we need new histograms: preempt_rate_by_egress_bucket and pack_efficiency_by_node_label so we can see if penalty actually improves packing.

lena: i'll add metrics: node.egress_5m, pod.preempt_count, node.pack_efficiency (tokens per GPU-hour).

anna: quick experiment: in staging i tried a heuristic patch that sorts candidate nodes by (gpu_free - egress_penalty) and saw a 12% improvement in contiguous gpu slices for fractional pods, and preemptions dropped 18%. will push logs to the thread later.

ji: nice. when we roll this, let's gate by canary on 5% of scheduler replicas and watch the new histograms + alert if preempt_rate increases > 5%.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout started for scheduler v2.3.4-canary on cluster staging (replicas: 2) :rocket:

anna: perfect — i'll attach the staging perf dump in a follow-up and we can decide on next steps after metrics look stable. :thumbsup:

mike: thanks team — agree to proceed with the prototype + metrics. if staging shows regressions, we'll abort the canary and revert scoring changes.

lena: cost note: burstpool 24/7 would add ~6% to infra spend for ap-southeast1, but with autoscaler we expect <1% steady increase and better tail latency. i'll include numbers in the doc.

anna: ok closing the loop here — saving action items to infra runbook. will file a follow-up RFC if staging is green.
